items.rationale: The concealed cold-water leak falls under §2.4.2 if escape-of-water cover is in force, and §7.1.7(e) covers the investigation needed to locate it. Allow €518 gross for one detection service.

Opening the partition for pipe access is covered under §7.1.7(a) and (g), and moving and propping shelving for access qualifies under §5.2.2. Allow €700 gross for eight hours of documented access and associated work.

items.description: Materials for partition access and repair
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(c) covers screws, tape and other minor consumables used for the covered work, and §7.1.10 permits a lump sum for them. Allow €129 gross.
The partition-access visit was a necessary attendance under §7.1.7(f), separate from the other trades' visits. Allow €84 gross.
The initial moisture map established 30 m² of affected space under §7.1.5. Section 7.1.7(b) covers necessary drying of that area at €457 gross, separate from the equipment hire.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers hire of a dryer suited to the affected area. Allow the first equipment charge at €444 gross.

items.description: Remove and dispose of 1 m² of insulation board
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(a) cover removal and disposal of the affected wall insulation board, distinct from the stud-bay wool; they do not cover the old condensation marks. Allow 1 m² at €86 gross.
Section 7.1.7(a) covers clearing the wet wool from the stud bays as an operation distinct from removing the wall insulation board. Allow €215 gross for the lot.

Sections 7.1.7(b) and 7.1.8(c) allow drying work attributable to the revised moisture map, but not rebilling the initial 30 m². Allow €300 gross for the additional roughly 20 m² and the work needed to extend drying to it.

Section 7.1.8(f) permits only one charge for the same dryer, even when moved to serve a larger area. The owner's unit was not invoiced, so €444 is only the conditional value of a separate eligible hire.

The blower was placed beside the charged dryer to assist the same drying operation, so §7.1.8(f) deems it included. If a distinct necessary use were established, the conditional allowance would be €28 gross.
The first repaired stretch required five bends, so these fittings correspond to the documented installation under §7.1.7(c). Allow five at €10.20 gross each.

The second repaired stretch needed its own five bends, and the different model is explained by stock availability. Under §§7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(c), allow five at €10 gross each, not as a duplicate of position 13.

Section 7.1.8(e) excludes material of a dimension that does not match the documented repair: the job used 15 mm copper, and no 28 mm line was opened. A matching claim for one such elbow would be worth about €20 gross.

items.description: Three metres of temporary bypass hose
items.rationale: Under §§7.1.1(b) and 7.1.8(e), a hose used only to keep the washing machine running is not a necessary repair cost. If shown necessary for the repair itself, allow €24 gross for 3 m.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers customary helper labour for the documented pipe works. The comparable five-hour line in Case 76 supports €239 gross.
The initial repair and the return visit to pressure-test and repair the second leak were distinct necessary attendances under §§7.1.7(f) and 7.1.8(c). Allow two at €84 gross each.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers the documented two transitions on the first repair and one additional transition on the second. Allow three at €23 gross each.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers customary labour for the pipe repairs and pressure testing. The 5.5-hour comparison in Case 76 supports €458 gross.
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(g) cover relaying the tiles loosened by the leak in both cellar areas, not tiling unaffected flooring. Allow 14 hours at €88 gross per hour.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 cover like-for-like installation materials. Allow €95 gross for adhesive and grout only, with no purchase allowance for the owner's spare tiles.
The tiler's visit was a separate necessary attendance for reinstatement under §7.1.7(f). Allow €84 gross.
